findings.body: The booking list exposes the action to team administrators, but the mutation returns FORBIDDEN even though the variable and existing listing authorization treat administrators and owners equivalently.
findings.failure_mode: Valid team administrators cannot add guests to bookings they manage.
findings.impact: The booking list exposes the action to team administrators, but the mutation returns FORBIDDEN even though the variable and existing listing authorization treat administrators and owners equivalently.
findings.root_cause: The administrator and owner predicates are intersected even though either role should grant access.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the result of isTeamAdmin directly because it already accepts ADMIN and OWNER, or combine separate role checks with OR rather than AND.
findings.title: Team administrators are rejected because the permission checks are combined with AND
findings.trigger: A user with the ADMIN role, but not OWNER, opens a team booking they do not personally organize or attend and invokes addGuests.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 47-48 shows `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. isTeamAdmin returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER roles per context L270, but isTeamOwner only returns true for OWNER per L286-294. AND-ing them means ADMIN-only users fail even though isTeamAdmin accepts them.

findings.body: EventManager cannot authenticate against the organizer's referenced calendars, so the attendee is stored in Cal.com while the organizer's external calendar event may remain unchanged or the mutation may fail after persisting the attendee.
findings.failure_mode: External calendar attendee lists diverge from the booking's attendee records for non-organizer callers.
findings.impact: EventManager cannot authenticate against the organizer's referenced calendars, so the attendee is stored in Cal.com while the organizer's external calendar event may remain unchanged or the mutation may fail after persisting the attendee.
findings.root_cause: The implementation conflates the authenticated actor with the owner of the external calendar resources.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve credentials for the booking organizer and any assigned collective hosts referenced by the booking, then construct EventManager from those hosts rather than ctx.user.
findings.title: Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the booking host's credentials
findings.trigger: An authorized attendee or team owner who is not the booking organizer adds a guest.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 158 shows `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetching caller's credentials, then line 160-163 creates EventManager with those. For non-organizer callers, these credentials won't authenticate against organizer's calendar, causing calendar update failures or no-ops.

findings.body: The existing attendee is still present in the raw guests array and is incorrectly sent a normal booking confirmation instead of the guest-added update email.
findings.failure_mode: Recipients are assigned the wrong email template based on guests that were not actually inserted.
findings.impact: The existing attendee is still present in the raw guests array and is incorrectly sent a normal booking confirmation instead of the guest-added update email.
findings.root_cause: Notification logic receives the original input after the persistence layer has filtered that input.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the normalized, deduplicated uniqueGuests list to sendAddGuestsEmails.
findings.title: Email classification uses the unfiltered request instead of the guests actually added
findings.trigger: A request contains one existing attendee and at least one genuinely new guest.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 168 passes raw `guests` array to sendAddGuestsEmails, but uniqueGuests (filtered list) was used for DB insert. Existing attendees in guests array get wrong email template per email-manager.ts L541-544 logic.

findings.body: The template literal remains truthy and produces text such as "undefined: Failed to fetch", so unable_to_add_guests is never used.
findings.failure_mode: Users see malformed low-level error text instead of the intended localized fallback.
findings.impact: The template literal remains truthy and produces text such as "undefined: Failed to fetch", so unable_to_add_guests is never used.
findings.root_cause: A template literal is treated as nullable even though it always creates a non-empty string.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the detailed message only when the relevant fields exist; otherwise pass t("unable_to_add_guests") directly.
findings.title: The error-toast fallback is unreachable and can show an undefined prefix
findings.trigger: A network-level tRPC failure has no err.data code or lacks a useful translated message.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 43 shows template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which always produces a truthy string even when code is undefined. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is unreachable.

raw_findings.title: Team administrators are rejected because the permission checks are combined with AND
raw_findings.trigger: A user with the ADMIN role, but not OWNER, opens a team booking they do not personally organize or attend and invokes addGuests.

raw_findings.body: EventManager cannot authenticate against the organizer's referenced calendars, so the attendee is stored in Cal.com while the organizer's external calendar event may remain unchanged or the mutation may fail after persisting the attendee.
raw_findings.failure_mode: External calendar attendee lists diverge from the booking's attendee records for non-organizer callers.
raw_findings.impact: EventManager cannot authenticate against the organizer's referenced calendars, so the attendee is stored in Cal.com while the organizer's external calendar event may remain unchanged or the mutation may fail after persisting the attendee.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation conflates the authenticated actor with the owner of the external calendar resources.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Resolve credentials for the booking organizer and any assigned collective hosts referenced by the booking, then construct EventManager from those hosts rather than ctx.user.
raw_findings.title: Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the booking host's credentials
raw_findings.trigger: An authorized attendee or team owner who is not the booking organizer adds a guest.

raw_findings.body: The request fails but the new attendee rows remain persisted; retrying can then report that no new guests are available, while the external calendar and notification state remain stale.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A single mutation leaves partially applied guest additions across the database and calendar providers.
raw_findings.impact: The request fails but the new attendee rows remain persisted; retrying can then report that no new guests are available, while the external calendar and notification state remain stale.
raw_findings.root_cause: A durable database write precedes an external side effect with no transaction-like recovery strategy.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Implement a compensating rollback or durable outbox/saga around the database and calendar operations so a failed external update is retried or the newly created rows are removed consistently.
raw_findings.title: The database is mutated before a fallible calendar update without compensation
raw_findings.trigger: A calendar provider rejects or times out during updateCalendarAttendees after the Prisma update succeeds.

raw_findings.body: createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows because the database has no booking/email uniqueness constraint, producing duplicate calendar attendees and notifications.
raw_findings.failure_mode: One API request can create multiple attendee records for the same mailbox.
raw_findings.impact: createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows because the database has no booking/email uniqueness constraint, producing duplicate calendar attendees and notifications.
raw_findings.root_cause: Uniqueness validation exists only in the UI and is omitted from the authoritative server schema.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce case-insensitive uniqueness in ZAddGuestsInputSchema and defensively deduplicate normalized addresses in the handler.
raw_findings.title: The server schema accepts duplicate guest addresses in one request
raw_findings.trigger: A direct tRPC caller submits the same email more than once, bypassing the dialog's client-only uniqueness refinement.

raw_findings.body: The existing attendee is not recognized and a second attendee row is inserted for the same mailbox, resulting in duplicate invites and attendee entries.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Semantically identical email addresses are treated as different attendees.
raw_findings.impact: The existing attendee is not recognized and a second attendee row is inserted for the same mailbox, resulting in duplicate invites and attendee entries.
raw_findings.root_cause: Email identity is tested with raw, case-sensitive string equality.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize both submitted and stored addresses before comparison, using the repository's canonical email-normalization rules.
raw_findings.title: Existing attendees are compared case-sensitively
raw_findings.trigger: A request supplies an existing attendee address with different letter casing, such as User@example.com instead of user@example.com.

raw_findings.body: The blocked mailbox is added as an attendee and can receive booking details despite the configured blacklist.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Configured guest-email restrictions are bypassed by equivalent address spellings.
raw_findings.impact: The blocked mailbox is added as an attendee and can receive booking details despite the configured blacklist.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only blacklist entries are lowercased; submitted addresses are compared verbatim and their base address is not extracted.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Trim and normalize both sides and compare extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() against normalized blacklist entries, matching the existing booking blacklist logic.
raw_findings.title: Blacklist checks can be bypassed with casing or plus-address aliases
raw_findings.trigger: A caller submits a blacklisted address with uppercase characters or a plus alias, while BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains its lowercase base address.

raw_findings.body: Both requests can pass the pre-insert filter and both create an attendee row because no database uniqueness constraint protects bookingId/email.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Racing requests persist duplicate attendee records and send duplicate updates.
raw_findings.impact: Both requests can pass the pre-insert filter and both create an attendee row because no database uniqueness constraint protects bookingId/email.
raw_findings.root_cause: Uniqueness is implemented as an application-level read-before-write check without database enforcement.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a case-normalized uniqueness constraint for attendee email within a booking and use an atomic upsert or conflict-skipping insert with a deterministic response.
raw_findings.title: Concurrent additions can race and create duplicate attendees
raw_findings.trigger: Two authorized callers concurrently add the same previously absent email to one booking.

raw_findings.body: The existing attendee is still present in the raw guests array and is incorrectly sent a normal booking confirmation instead of the guest-added update email.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Recipients are assigned the wrong email template based on guests that were not actually inserted.
raw_findings.impact: The existing attendee is still present in the raw guests array and is incorrectly sent a normal booking confirmation instead of the guest-added update email.
raw_findings.root_cause: Notification logic receives the original input after the persistence layer has filtered that input.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the normalized, deduplicated uniqueGuests list to sendAddGuestsEmails.
raw_findings.title: Email classification uses the unfiltered request instead of the guests actually added
raw_findings.trigger: A request contains one existing attendee and at least one genuinely new guest.

raw_findings.body: Organizer and attendee emails are sent anyway, violating the event type's configured notification policy and potentially sending messages workflows intended to suppress.
raw_findings.evidence: export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[]) => {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Disabled standard notifications are delivered despite explicit event-type settings.
raw_findings.impact: Organizer and attendee emails are sent anyway, violating the event type's configured notification policy and potentially sending messages workflows intended to suppress.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new email function has no metadata parameter and unconditionally schedules every recipient email.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Accept event-type metadata, pass booking.eventType.metadata from the handler, and guard host and attendee sends with eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail as sendLocationChangeEmails does.
raw_findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore event-type email suppression settings
raw_findings.trigger: Guests are added to an event type whose metadata disables standard host or attendee emails.

raw_findings.body: The request performs a bulk insert, resolves translations for every resulting attendee, updates calendar integrations, and attempts thousands of emails, enabling resource exhaustion and outbound-email abuse.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A single authenticated request can consume excessive database, translation, calendar, and email resources.
raw_findings.impact: The request performs a bulk insert, resolves translations for every resulting attendee, updates calendar integrations, and attempts thousands of emails, enabling resource exhaustion and outbound-email abuse.
raw_findings.root_cause: The mutation accepts an unbounded collection while each element triggers database and external side effects.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Apply a documented .min(1) and conservative .max(...) limit in the server schema and rate-limit repeated guest additions per user and booking.
raw_findings.title: The guest array has no server-side size limit
raw_findings.trigger: An authorized or compromised attendee submits thousands of valid email addresses in one mutation.

raw_findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails sees calendarEvent.team as undefined, so its team-member notification branch never runs and co-hosts do not receive the guest-added update.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Only the primary organizer is notified for team bookings even though the email manager explicitly supports team recipients.
raw_findings.impact: sendAddGuestsEmails sees calendarEvent.team as undefined, so its team-member notification branch never runs and co-hosts do not receive the guest-added update.
raw_findings.root_cause: The handler builds a standalone CalendarEvent without the team relation expected by the new email manager.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Query the assigned team hosts and populate evt.team with their Person details before invoking calendar and email updates.
raw_findings.title: The constructed CalendarEvent never includes team members
raw_findings.trigger: A guest is added to a collective or other team booking with additional host members.

raw_findings.body: The event sent to new guests lacks videoCallData, so their calendar/email invitation can omit the meeting URL or credentials.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Guests added to affected conferencing integrations receive incomplete joining information.
raw_findings.impact: The event sent to new guests lacks videoCallData, so their calendar/email invitation can omit the meeting URL or credentials.
raw_findings.root_cause: The reference predicate implements only one of the two supported video-integration naming conventions.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Recognize both video and conferencing reference types using the same integration classification used by EventManager.
raw_findings.title: Conferencing references are excluded when deriving video-call data
raw_findings.trigger: A booking uses an integration whose reference type ends in _conferencing rather than containing _video.

raw_findings.body: The caller receives a successful guest-added response even though the new guest may receive no invitation, and the actual error is discarded so the delivery cannot be diagnosed or retried.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Guest records are created without a reliable notification and operators have no actionable failure record.
raw_findings.impact: The caller receives a successful guest-added response even though the new guest may receive no invitation, and the actual error is discarded so the delivery cannot be diagnosed or retried.
raw_findings.root_cause: The handler catches all notification errors, discards their details, and continues to the success response.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Queue notification delivery through a retryable job/outbox and log the actual error; expose a partial-delivery status if reliable retry cannot be guaranteed.
raw_findings.title: Email delivery failures are swallowed while the mutation reports success
raw_findings.trigger: SMTP or email rendering fails after guests and calendar attendees have been updated, especially for a booking without a calendar integration that could send its own invitation.

raw_findings.body: The message is delivered to the team member's address but the rendered organizer template is personalized with the primary organizer and has no teamMember context.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Team recipients receive an email addressed or contextualized for another host.
raw_findings.impact: The message is delivered to the team member's address but the rendered organizer template is personalized with the primary organizer and has no teamMember context.
raw_findings.root_cause: The recipient is used for the mail envelope but omitted from the React template props.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass teamMember: this.teamMember to renderEmail, matching OrganizerScheduledEmail's payload.
raw_findings.title: Team-member emails omit the teamMember personalization prop
raw_findings.trigger: sendAddGuestsEmails receives a CalendarEvent with team members and constructs OrganizerAddGuestsEmail with a teamMember.

raw_findings.title: Correcting an invalid address leaves the validation warning visible
raw_findings.trigger: The user submits an invalid or duplicate address, then edits the field to a valid unique address.

raw_findings.trigger: A user enters addresses or triggers validation and closes the dialog with Escape, the overlay, or the close control before reopening it.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Query the assigned team hosts and populate evt.team with their Person details before invoking calendar and email updates.
validated_findings.title: The constructed CalendarEvent never includes team members
validated_findings.trigger: A guest is added to a collective or other team booking with additional host members.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 124-147 constructs CalendarEvent without team property. sendAddGuestsEmails at L531-537 checks calendarEvent.team?.members for team notifications, so co-hosts won't receive emails.

validated_findings.body: The event sent to new guests lacks videoCallData, so their calendar/email invitation can omit the meeting URL or credentials.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Guests added to affected conferencing integrations receive incomplete joining information.
validated_findings.impact: The event sent to new guests lacks videoCallData, so their calendar/email invitation can omit the meeting URL or credentials.
validated_findings.root_cause: The reference predicate implements only one of the two supported video-integration naming conventions.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Recognize both video and conferencing reference types using the same integration classification used by EventManager.
validated_findings.title: Conferencing references are excluded when deriving video-call data
validated_findings.trigger: A booking uses an integration whose reference type ends in _conferencing rather than containing _video.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 122 shows `reference.type.includes("_video")`. EventManager.ts L126 shows videoCredentials filter includes `_conferencing` suffix. Conferencing integrations would be missed by the _video check.

validated_findings.body: The caller receives a successful guest-added response even though the new guest may receive no invitation, and the actual error is discarded so the delivery cannot be diagnosed or retried.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Guest records are created without a reliable notification and operators have no actionable failure record.
validated_findings.impact: The caller receives a successful guest-added response even though the new guest may receive no invitation, and the actual error is discarded so the delivery cannot be diagnosed or retried.
validated_findings.root_cause: The handler catches all notification errors, discards their details, and continues to the success response.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Queue notification delivery through a retryable job/outbox and log the actual error; expose a partial-delivery status if reliable retry cannot be guaranteed.
validated_findings.title: Email delivery failures are swallowed while the mutation reports success
validated_findings.trigger: SMTP or email rendering fails after guests and calendar attendees have been updated, especially for a booking without a calendar integration that could send its own invitation.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 167-171 show catch block logs generic message and continues to return success. Email failures are silently swallowed with no retry mechanism, leaving guests without invitations while reporting success.

validated_findings.body: The message is delivered to the team member's address but the rendered organizer template is personalized with the primary organizer and has no teamMember context.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Team recipients receive an email addressed or contextualized for another host.
validated_findings.impact: The message is delivered to the team member's address but the rendered organizer template is personalized with the primary organizer and has no teamMember context.
validated_findings.root_cause: The recipient is used for the mail envelope but omitted from the React template props.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass teamMember: this.teamMember to renderEmail, matching OrganizerScheduledEmail's payload.
validated_findings.title: Team-member emails omit the teamMember personalization prop
validated_findings.trigger: sendAddGuestsEmails receives a CalendarEvent with team members and constructs OrganizerAddGuestsEmail with a teamMember.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 31-34 shows renderEmail called with only `attendee: this.calEvent.organizer` and `calEvent`. Compare to OrganizerScheduledEmail L51-56 which passes `teamMember` prop. Team member personalization is missing.

validated_findings.body: The emails_must_be_unique_valid warning remains visible while the current input is valid, giving contradictory validation feedback.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The dialog displays a stale error after the user has corrected the input.
validated_findings.impact: The emails_must_be_unique_valid warning remains visible while the current input is valid, giving contradictory validation feedback.
validated_findings.root_cause: Input changes update only the email array and never reset the failed-validation state.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap setValue so any edit clears isInvalidEmail, or derive validation state from the current value instead of retaining a sticky boolean.
validated_findings.title: Correcting an invalid address leaves the validation warning visible
validated_findings.trigger: The user submits an invalid or duplicate address, then edits the field to a valid unique address.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 73 shows setValue={setMultiEmailValue} but no call to setIsInvalidEmail(false) on value change. isInvalidEmail state persists after correction, showing stale validation error.

validated_findings.body: The prior addresses and validation warning reappear, unlike the explicit Cancel path which clears them.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Equivalent close actions leave the dialog in inconsistent states on its next open.
validated_findings.impact: The prior addresses and validation warning reappear, unlike the explicit Cancel path which clears them.
validated_findings.root_cause: Only the custom Cancel and success paths reset local state; generic Dialog close events directly toggle visibility.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Handle onOpenChange with a wrapper that resets multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail whenever the dialog transitions to closed.
validated_findings.title: Closing the dialog outside the Cancel button preserves stale form state
validated_findings.trigger: A user enters addresses or triggers validation and closes the dialog with Escape, the overlay, or the close control before reopening it.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 61 shows Dialog with onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog} but no state reset. Cancel button at lines 89-94 resets state, but closing via overlay/escape doesn't, leaving stale form state.

validated_findings.body: The button produces no validation message, request, or explanation, making the dialog appear broken.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A reachable UI state turns the primary action into an unexplained no-op.
validated_findings.impact: The button produces no validation message, request, or explanation, making the dialog appear broken.
validated_findings.root_cause: The empty-list path exits before either validation feedback or mutation execution.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Disable Add while the list is empty, preserve at least one input row, or set a required-email validation error instead of returning silently.
validated_findings.title: Removing every field makes Add silently do nothing
validated_findings.trigger: The user removes the only email field and then clicks Add.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 48-51 show early return when multiEmailValue.length === 0 with no feedback. Button remains enabled but does nothing, confusing users who removed all fields.

validated_findings.body: The template literal remains truthy and produces text such as "undefined: Failed to fetch", so unable_to_add_guests is never used.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Users see malformed low-level error text instead of the intended localized fallback.
validated_findings.impact: The template literal remains truthy and produces text such as "undefined: Failed to fetch", so unable_to_add_guests is never used.
validated_findings.root_cause: A template literal is treated as nullable even though it always creates a non-empty string.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Build the detailed message only when the relevant fields exist; otherwise pass t("unable_to_add_guests") directly.
validated_findings.title: The error-toast fallback is unreachable and can show an undefined prefix
validated_findings.trigger: A network-level tRPC failure has no err.data code or lacks a useful translated message.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 43 shows template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which always produces a truthy string even when code is undefined. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is unreachable.

validated_findings.body: No EmailField is assigned id="emails", so the visible label does not name or focus the input controls; multiple fields are exposed without a programmatic group label.
validated_findings.evidence: <label htmlFor="emails" className="text-default my-2 block text-sm font-medium">
validated_findings.failure_mode: Assistive technology cannot reliably associate the displayed label with the email inputs.
validated_findings.impact: No EmailField is assigned id="emails", so the visible label does not name or focus the input controls; multiple fields are exposed without a programmatic group label.
validated_findings.root_cause: The label uses a hard-coded htmlFor value that is never supplied to the rendered EmailField elements.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Give each field a stable unique id and associate labels correctly, or wrap the collection in a fieldset with a legend.
validated_findings.title: The visible email label is not associated with any input
validated_findings.trigger: A screen-reader or label-click user interacts with a MultiEmail instance.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 21 shows `<label htmlFor="emails">` but EmailField components at lines 27-53 have no id="emails" attribute. Label association is broken for accessibility.

validated_findings.body: The otherwise localized component displays an English-only tooltip.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The new control is only partially localized.
validated_findings.impact: The otherwise localized component displays an English-only tooltip.
validated_findings.root_cause: User-facing tooltip text is hard-coded instead of using the locale hook already present in the component.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a remove_email translation key and render it through t(...).
validated_findings.title: The remove-email tooltip bypasses localization
validated_findings.trigger: A user runs the application in any non-English locale and focuses or hovers the remove control.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Hardcoded English tooltip is a stylistic/i18n issue, not a functional bug. The component works correctly; this is a localization improvement suggestion rather than a defect.

validated_findings.body: The identifier and matching add_members test selector conflate booking guests with team members, making selectors and telemetry misleading and increasing the chance of collisions with actual member-management actions.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Code and tests describe guest addition as team membership management.
validated_findings.impact: The identifier and matching add_members test selector conflate booking guests with team members, making selectors and telemetry misleading and increasing the chance of collisions with actual member-management actions.
validated_findings.root_cause: Internal identifiers use a different domain entity from the user-visible feature and server API.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the action id and dialog test selector consistently to add_guests.
validated_findings.title: Guest actions are internally named as member actions
validated_findings.trigger: Tests or maintainers search for or extend the additional-guests action alongside team-member management features.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a stylistic/naming preference issue. The id 'add_members' is used internally for an action that adds guests. While the naming could be clearer, this is not a functional defect - the label correctly shows t('additional_guests') to users, and the internal id is just for programmatic identification. No concrete bug, security issue, or functional failure results from this naming choice.

validated_findings.body: There is no added test exercising organizer, attendee, ADMIN, OWNER, and unrelated-user access or asserting database/calendar/email behavior, allowing authorization and partial-update regressions in this new mutation to ship undetected.
validated_findings.evidence: export const addGuestsHandler = async ({ ctx, input }: AddGuestsOptions) => {
validated_findings.failure_mode: CI cannot verify the mutation's authorization and consistency contract.
validated_findings.impact: There is no added test exercising organizer, attendee, ADMIN, OWNER, and unrelated-user access or asserting database/calendar/email behavior, allowing authorization and partial-update regressions in this new mutation to ship undetected.
validated_findings.root_cause: A security- and integration-sensitive endpoint was added without corresponding automated tests.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add handler tests with mocked Prisma, EventManager, and email delivery covering the full role matrix, normalized duplicate/blacklist handling, and external-side-effect failures.
validated_findings.title: The new authorization boundary has no handler-level regression tests
validated_findings.trigger: The permission logic, email filtering, or side-effect ordering changes and the test suite runs before merge.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage suggestion, not a defect in the patch. The candidate claims there are no tests for the new addGuestsHandler, but absence of tests is a process/coverage concern, not a bug introduced by the patch. The handler itself contains authorization checks (isTeamAdmin, isTeamOwner, booking.userId checks). The finding is speculative about potential regressions rather than identifying an actual defect in the changed code.
